text:
kevin: quick triage ping — we started seeing a spike in OOMs on dedicated-prod-gpu after the quant-2bit rollout last night. ~8/12 nodes had at least one process killed, RSS shot up before oom. Can we gather heapshots and run a quick bisect?
priya: ack. which service and commit? any perf/regress correlates?
jordan: service: runtime-infer-v2 (s3). Commit: f3ad9c8 -> quant patch + new allocator tweak. Bench-run last night showed ~6% latency tail increase for long-context workloads.
kevin: thanks. logs show: 
```
[2026-03-16T22:14:32Z] infer[pid=2345]: Alloc failed: 1.2G, RSS 13.4G, VM 42G
[2026-03-16T22:14:33Z] oom-killer: killed process 2345 (infer) total-vm:42000000kB
```
priya: ok can someone capture a heapshot on a repro node? ideal flow: reproduce with load, run heapshot, upload to s3; then try reverting quant change to confirm.
sven: I can grab one from canary-3 (same hw/driver). command I use: 
```
sudo heapshot capture --pid=$(pgrep -f runtime-infer) --out /tmp/heapshot-$(date +%s).gz
aws s3 cp /tmp/heapshot-*.gz s3://redwood-debug/heapshots/1903456789/
```
sven: also plan to grab /proc/vmstat, smaps before/after the spike.
kevin: perfect. can you also run the smallalloc stress binary from bench harness? suspect fragmentation + quant cache growth.
sven: will run: `./tools/bench_smallalloc --duration=300 --threads=4 --alloc-size-dist=longtail` and attach results.
bench-bot: nightly-bench: throughput -2.1% (long-context, quant-2bit), p99 latency +6.3% compared to baseline. See /bench/runs/2026-03-16/quant-2bit.json
jordan: if fragmentation is the cause, we might see growing number of arenas and high per-arena RSS. can someone run `malloc_info` endpoint on the node? runtime exposes /debug/malloc?show with JSON.
priya: I've queued a bisect on canary: reverting the allocator tweak only (keep quant) vs reverting quant only. will spin up paired runs. timeline ~2-3h.
kevin: good. priority: 1) collect heapshot + smaps, 2) run malloc_info, 3) bisect runs, 4) if repro is easy, try `MALLOC_CONF=prof:true,lg_prof_interval:...` to get sampling.
sven: uploaded heapshot and smaps to s3://redwood-debug/heapshots/1903456789/heapshot-canary3.gz and smaps.txt. Also attached smallalloc bench logs.
ops-oncall: FYI I bumped dedicated-prod-gpu pool to allow more headroom and drained two worst nodes to prevent customer impact. No SLA hits so far.
kevin: thanks Ops. once we have heapshot + malloc_info we can inspect for retained large chunks from KV cache or prefix KVC. jordan can you run heap-analysis?
jordan: on it. preliminary grep shows a lot of mmap allocations ~1-4M coming from kvcache.c:kv_shard_alloc. sketch: the quant codec increases per-token cache footprint because of slower compaction.
priya: interesting — quant-cache compaction interaction with allocator. can you share a flame/stack histogram from heapshot?
jordan: attached histograms -> top frames: 
- kvcache.c:kv_shard_alloc (45% retained)
- tokenizer.c:tokenizer_decode (12%)
- runtime/beam_search.c (8%)

jordan: hypothesis: quant-2bit increases cache block size, causing more fragmentation in smallalloc pools. If the allocator tweak changed slab reuse thresholds, we may be leaking into new arenas and not reclaiming.
kevin: good hypothesis. Priya — if bisect shows reverting quant fixes OOMs, we'll need an immediate rollback for prod with a patch to compaction or allocator thresholds.
priya: agree. bisect running: revert-quant job completed -> no OOMs in repro window. revert-alloc job (revert allocator tweak) -> still saw one oom. preliminary verdict: quant change is primary culprit.
sven: I can test a mitigation: enable aggressive kvcache compaction after each request for a canary run (cheap flag). small perf cost but may reduce fragmentation. I'll run canary-flagged build.
bench-bot: canary-run-190345: quant-2bit + compaction-agg -> p99 improved vs baseline, throughput -1.5%.
kevin: roll-back plan: 1) rollback quant-2bit in prod -> immediate 2) schedule safer quant rollout with compaction/allocator tweaks in staging and perf windows. Priya, Jordan, can you prepare a postmortem blameless summary? Include heapshots, bisect results, bench outputs, and recommended next steps.
priya: will draft. Jordan collecting heap analysis artifacts and graphs.
kevin: thanks all. please @me when draft is ready. :thumbsup:
